solution: Let $g(x)=\dfrac{|\cos x|}{|\sin x|+|\cos x|}$; $\sin(2\pi-x)=-\sin x$, $\cos(2\pi-x)=\cos x$, so $g(2\pi-x)=g(x)$
(Equivalently, with $t=x-\pi$, $(t-\sin t)g$ is odd on $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$ and integrates to $0$)
$\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}g=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\frac{|\cos t|}{|\sin t|+|\cos t|}dt=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\cos t}{\sin t+\cos t}dt$ (even integrand)
King's rule: $\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\cos t}{\sin t+\cos t}dt=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sin t}{\sin t+\cos t}dt=\frac{\pi}{4}$
solution_full: Write $g(x)=\dfrac{|\cos x|}{|\sin x|+|\cos x|}$, so $I=\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}(x+\sin x)g(x)\,dx$.
Since $\sin(2\pi-x)=-\sin x$ and $\cos(2\pi-x)=\cos x$, we have $g(2\pi-x)=g(x)$.
Adding the two forms of $I$: $2I=\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}2\pi\,g(x)\,dx$, so $I=\pi\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}g(x)\,dx$.

The same conclusion through odd and even functions: put $x=\pi+t$; then $x+\sin x=\pi+(t-\sin t)$ and $g(\pi+t)=\dfrac{|\cos t|}{|\sin t|+|\cos t|}$ is even in $t$, while $(t-\sin t)$ is odd, so their product integrates to $0$ over $[-\pi/2,\pi/2]$.

Now $\int_{\pi/2}^{3\pi/2}g(x)\,dx=\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{|\cos t|}{|\sin t|+|\cos t|}dt=2\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos t}{\sin t+\cos t}dt$, because the integrand is even and on $[0,\pi/2]$ both $\sin t,\cos t\ge0$.

Let $J=\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos t}{\sin t+\cos t}dt$. King's rule ($t\to\pi/2-t$) gives $J=\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\sin t}{\cos t+\sin t}dt$; adding, $2J=\int_0^{\pi/2}1\,dt=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, so $J=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
originality_note: New: the weight x + sin x is split as a constant plus a part odd about x = pi, on an interval centred at pi, and the remaining modulus integrand reduces to a king pair (way 5). Closest known: int_0^pi x f(sin x) dx = (pi/2) int_0^pi f(sin x) dx. Different because: the interval is [pi/2, 3pi/2], the weight contains sin x, and the moduli must be handled before the king pair appears.
